chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Umar ibn Hanzalah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He stipulates for her whatever days he wishes.

key_terms.الْأَيَّامِ: The days (referring to the period of the contract)
key_terms.يُشَارِطُهَا: He stipulates for her (referring to the duration)

ai.seo_question: What is the rule regarding the duration stipulation in temporary marriage according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This brief hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the flexibility of the time stipulation (ajal) in temporary marriage (mut'ah), affirming that the husband may specify any duration he chooses. In Shia jurisprudence, this supports the view that the minimum period is not strictly fixed by the Prophet but is determined by mutual agreement, distinguishing it from permanent marriage. The narration underscores the contractual nature of mut'ah, where the duration is a key element of validity rather than a fixed ritual constraint.
